questions.question: Should you edit your profile from the 'Liked You' screen or return to browsing?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to edit your profile to attract more attention, but viewing the actual likes typically requires a premium subscription.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the agency to decide whether to ignore this premium-gated section and continue browsing for free.
questions.check: What does the liked-you screen prompt, and what does it show without paying?
questions.say_example: Back to the feed. The edit-your-profile nag on the likes screen is just a nag.

questions.question: Which of the people who already liked you do you want to review further?
questions.why: The screen displays a grid of users who have already liked your profile along with their ages and relationship goals, letting you prioritize reviewing guaranteed matches.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to personally evaluate the physical attractiveness and vibe of the candidates who have already shown interest in you.
questions.check: Which users does the liked-you grid show, with what details?
questions.say_example: Went through the people who liked you first - a like back there is a match straight away.

questions.question: Do you want to inspect the profiles of the people who visited you?
questions.why: The screen reveals a list of users like '[username]' and '[username]' who viewed your profile, presenting an opportunity to evaluate them or navigate away.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to personally decide whether to pursue a connection with someone who has already shown interest by visiting their profile.
questions.check: Which visitors does the page list?
questions.say_example: Visitor names (<[username], [username]>) are in the report.

questions.question: Do you have any pending messages that require a reply?
questions.why: The 'Your turn' tab shows "You're all caught up," confirming there are no real matches waiting for a response, making the automated introductory message safe to ignore.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to quickly distinguish between automated system greetings and genuine messages from potential matches.
questions.check: What does the your-turn tab say is pending?
questions.say_example: The your-turn tab says all caught up. The only unread thing was the app's own auto-message.

questions.question: Do you notice the app warns 'Can't change it later,' then shows an 'Edit name' button anyway?
questions.why: The interface contradicts itself by warning that your name cannot be changed later, only to immediately offer an edit button on the confirmation pop-up.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of this unexpected final grace period to correct a typo in your permanent profile name.
questions.check: What did the warning say about changing the name, and what does the confirmation pop-up offer?
questions.say_example: The page swore the name can't change later, then offered an Edit button on the next pop-up. So the warning is only half true.

questions.question: Are you okay with the contradictory privacy terms regarding how your dating activity is shared across Facebook?
questions.why: The initial setup screen claims your activity will not be shared outside of Dating, but the final confirmation states it will be used to personalize ads across other Facebook products.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating to an agent means you lose the opportunity to catch this privacy contradiction and decide if you are truly comfortable with your dating data being used for Facebook ads.
questions.check: What does each screen say about dating activity being shared outside the dating section?
questions.say_example: Two screens disagree about your privacy. The first said your dating activity stays inside Dating. The final one says it shapes ads across <the company's other apps>. The second is what you'd be agreeing to.

questions.question: Are you actually getting the exact discount advertised on the subscription plan?
questions.why: The Tinder Plus 6-month plan claims a 50% discount off the 1-month price, but the listed price of NPR 1,948.90 is slightly higher than a true 50% discount.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to notice minor pricing discrepancies and make a fully informed financial decision before subscribing.
questions.check: What discount does the page claim, and what are the listed prices for each plan?
questions.say_example: The <6-month> plan says half off, but its listed price lands above a true half. The real number is <price shown>.

questions.question: Did you notice that you can proceed without entering the supposedly required email and phone number?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that an email and phone number are required to secure the profile, yet the form allows submission with both fields left completely blank.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the intended account security and recovery options if the agent skips providing contact details that the platform claims are necessary.
questions.check: Does the page mark the email and phone fields required, and did submission succeed with them empty?
questions.say_example: The form called email and phone required, then accepted both blank. Logged the contradiction.

questions.question: Does the profile completion percentage decrease after you add photos and interests?
questions.why: The completion indicator drops to 25% after adding information, contradicting the 45% shown before editing began.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses certainty that their profile updates were actually saved and recognized by the platform.
questions.check: What completion percentage does the page show before and after the additions?
questions.say_example: The completion meter fell from <45%> to <25%> after adding things. It's a sales meter, not a measurement.

questions.question: Can you switch to BFF or Bizz mode in settings after finishing setup?
questions.why: The onboarding screen explicitly states that mode switching is locked until setup is complete, making it important to verify that the settings menu later allows this change.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the direct confirmation that your new account is fully unlocked and capable of toggling between dating, friendship, and business modes.
questions.check: Does the settings menu now offer the mode switch the onboarding said was locked?
questions.say_example: Checked later - the mode switch the onboarding promised does unlock after setup.

questions.question: Do you notice the discrepancy between the 'All 3' tab count and the four blurred profile cards shown in the grid?
questions.why: Recognizing this mismatch helps you realize the app is likely displaying a generic loading skeleton rather than an accurate grid of your actual likes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might misinterpret the generic placeholder grid as actual profiles, leading to confusion about exactly how many people have liked your account.
questions.check: What count does the tab label show, and how many cards does the grid draw?
questions.say_example: The likes tab said <3>, the grid drew <4> blurred cards. The grid is a placeholder, not your likes.

questions.question: Did the discovery feed completely ignore the maximum distance filter you just set?
questions.why: The user explicitly restricted the distance to 49 miles, but the very first profile shown is 744 miles away, indicating the app's location filtering silently failed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might trust the app's settings and waste time evaluating candidates who are geographically impossible to meet because the filter didn't actually apply.
questions.check: What maximum distance do your settings show, and what distance does the shown profile list?
questions.say_example: Your limit says <49> miles. The first profile the feed dealt is <744> miles out. The filter isn't holding - I'll check the outside-your-preferences switch and set it right before we go on.

questions.question: Are the profiles you liked appearing in the 'Intros' tab as the app claims?
questions.why: The 'Intros' tab states that liked profiles will appear there, but it remains empty even though the 'You Like' tab confirms two profiles were liked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses clarity on the status of their outgoing likes if the agent ignores the discrepancy between the two tabs.
questions.check: What does the Intros tab say it shows, and what does the You Like tab list?
questions.say_example: The app says your likes show up under Intros. You Like lists <two> people. Intros is empty. Your likes went somewhere - just not where it promised.

children.label: Start a conversation
children.note: 7.1 where the app makes you pick a channel or pay for one; it reaches into 5 when the message is what is gated. 7.2 then 7.3, repeated per match - MpoY writes four openers in one sitting, 1D06 four across two. 7.4 instead of 7.3 where the platform writes it. 7.5 and 7.6 once replies arrive, which needs another pass through 6. 7.7 only after the message has already gone.

questions.question: Does the bio text mention something on the stated dealbreaker list?
questions.why: The profile text reveals at the end that she is a mother, which introduces a major lifestyle factor that often acts as a personal dealbreaker.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent would likely process the profile based on surface-level stats and send a generic message, failing to apply your nuanced personal boundaries regarding dating someone with children.
questions.check: Does the profile's bio text mention children or another item from the stated dealbreaker list?
questions.say_example: One thing sitting at the bottom of her bio - <she's a mom>. You'd told me that's a line for you. Pass, or does this one get a different rule?

questions.question: Do you want to acknowledge that chat is restricted until your profile is screened?
questions.why: The app displays a pop-up stating that your profile must be screened by the platform before you can use the chat feature.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the direct notification that their messaging capabilities are temporarily delayed pending platform approval.
questions.check: What does the pop-up say about chat being restricted, and until when?
questions.say_example: The app is holding chat shut until it screens your profile. Nothing to press - messages unlock when their check clears.

questions.question: Did the message actually send, or is there a 'failed to send' error to retry?
questions.why: Dating apps frequently experience server hiccups or shadowbans that cause messages to fail silently or display a small error icon, meaning your match never received your opener.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might assume the task is complete the moment it clicks send, failing to notice the error state and leaving you thinking the match simply ignored you.
questions.check: Does the chat show a failed-to-send mark or error next to the last message?
questions.say_example: Your message to <name> shows a failed-to-send mark - it never reached her. Sending it again now.

questions.question: Did the match disappear from your queue right as you went to message them?
questions.why: A match can disappear instantly if the other person accidentally swiped right and immediately unmatched, or if the platform's automated moderation suddenly banned their account as a bot.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might fail the task trying to message a phantom profile, when a human would recognize the unmatch and simply return to the swiping queue.
questions.check: Which matches does the queue list now?
questions.say_example: <Name> is gone from your matches - the thread vanished before anything was sent. That's them unmatching, or the app pulling the account. Nothing went out.

questions.question: Which option should you choose to message this user?
questions.why: The profile page presents multiple contact methods, such as an envelope icon, a chat bubble, and an add friend button, which may trigger different communication flows.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the personal choice of how formally or casually you want to approach a potential match.
questions.check: Which contact controls does the profile page show?
questions.say_example: Used the plain chat path. The other buttons - <friend request, envelope> - do different things, noted in the report.

questions.question: Which of these recent matches will you message?
questions.why: Reviewing details like their ages, locations, and whether they are currently online helps you prioritize who to message and how to break the ice.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally evaluate their photos and craft an opening message based on your genuine, subjective attraction.
questions.check: Which matches does the list show, with what details?
questions.say_example: Worked through the matches in order - each opener still waits for your words.

questions.question: Which of these initial messages should you open and reply to first?
questions.why: The screen shows multiple matches like Courtney and [name] have already reached out with opening lines, requiring a decision on who to engage with.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally evaluate the opening lines and decide which match sparks their genuine interest.
questions.check: Which received messages does the list show, from whom?
questions.say_example: Queued the ones who wrote first. Their messages get read to you before any reply.

questions.question: Do you want to open any of these received messages to read them in full?
questions.why: The screen displays previews, senders, and dates for received messages, letting you decide if any are worth your time to open and engage with.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally evaluate the tone of the message previews and decide which senders actually pique your interest.
questions.check: What do the message previews show - sender, date, first line?
questions.say_example: Opened and read each message - replies only on your word.

questions.question: What should you say in your first message to a match?
questions.why: The chat interface requires an opening message, and personalizing it with the match's name or specific profile details can make a stronger first impression.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might send generic greetings instead of crafting personalized openers that reflect your unique conversational style and charm.
questions.check: What does the match's profile and any prior message show, and what does the page say about limits or deadlines on sending?
questions.say_example: Writing to <name> now - this speaks as you. Her profile mentions <a detail>. Tell me what to say, or I'll offer a draft and you approve it word for word.

questions.question: Does the page say connecting sends a default message, and what is its text?
questions.why: The app displays a generic default message for all connect requests and requires a paid upgrade to write your own.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether a personalized first impression is worth paying for.
questions.check: What default message does the page say a connect sends, and does changing it require an upgrade?
questions.say_example: One thing before this connect - it sends the site's stock line, <the message>, in your name. Writing your own is paywalled. Send their words, pay to write yours, or skip this one?

questions.question: What does her profile list for the detail you asked about?
questions.why: Scanning her profile for specific details like height helps you decide how to appropriately tailor your response.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the personal touch of evaluating her specific profile details and crafting a uniquely flirty reply that matches their own personality.
questions.check: What does the profile page list under height?
questions.say_example: Looked up the height on her profile - <listed value, or not listed>. The reply itself waited for your words.

questions.question: How should you reply to [name]'s story about her dog?
questions.why: The chat history shows [name] sharing a personal detail about her dog being scared of fireworks, presenting a clear opportunity to build rapport.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this reply means losing the chance to share a genuine personal anecdote and naturally steer the conversation toward a personalized date.
questions.check: What does the newest message in the thread say?
questions.say_example: She wrote - <her message, read out>. The reply should be in your words. Tell me what to send, or ask me for a draft to approve.

children.label: Leave the app
children.note: 8.1 is how every conversation that goes anywhere in this corpus ends - the other person offers a number or an Instagram handle, on the app's own screen, and the rest happens somewhere else. 8.2 then 8.3 on the one keeper that quits; 3yWz turns discovery off before deleting anything. no keeper does both.

questions.question: Does the latest exchange contain a phone number, an outside handle, or a request to move off the app?
questions.why: Reading her detailed response about climbing with her brothers helps you gauge her interest level and determine the success of your opening line.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might lack the social intuition to read the natural rhythm of this exchange and know exactly when to transition from casual banter to asking for contact information.
questions.check: Does the chat text contain a phone number, an outside handle, or a request to switch apps?
questions.say_example: The chat now has <a phone number> in it. Once you two move off the app, block and report stop working. I'm saying it once, then it's your call.

questions.question: Do you want to disable location-based discovery to hide your profile?
questions.why: The profile settings screen includes options to disable location tracking and hide your profile from other people's searches.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might leave your profile publicly visible to nearby users when you want to remain hidden.
questions.check: Which hiding controls does the settings screen show?
questions.say_example: Turned off location discovery, as you asked.

questions.question: How long do you want your profile to be invisible?
questions.why: The screen provides specific duration options like 24 hours, 72 hours, a week, or indefinitely for pausing your account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control exactly when your profile will become visible to other users again.
questions.check: Which pause lengths does the page offer?
questions.say_example: The app can hide you for <24 hours, 72 hours, a week>, or until you say otherwise. Nobody new sees you while it's on. How long?

questions.question: Did you exit the app after creating the profile instead of continuing to browse and match?
questions.why: The screen transitions to the phone's home screen right after the profile is created, indicating the task was stopped before interacting with any candidates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user receives a completed profile but no actual connections because the agent stopped before browsing or messaging anyone.
questions.check: Does the screen show the phone's home screen after the profile was created?
questions.say_example: Stopped after the profile went up, as asked - no browsing, no likes. The home screen was the last stop.
